gaps.sentence: We inspected the four bridges, but ___ of them was safe.
gaps.explanation: 'None of them was ...' is used for three or more items; 'neither' is only for two.

gaps.sentence: There were ___ than twenty people at the meeting.
We see our grandparents ___ other weekend.
gaps.explanation: 'Every other weekend' means alternate weekends; 'each other' has a different, reciprocal meaning.

gaps.sentence: There's ___ point asking him again — he never replies.
gaps.explanation: 'There's no point' — 'point' needs the adjective 'no', not the pronoun 'none'.

gaps.hint: the defined remainder of a known group
gaps.explanation: 'The others' refers to the specific remaining students; 'the other' is singular.

gaps.sentence: Three out of four respondents — that is, the ___ — supported the change.
gaps.hint: three out of four = more than half
gaps.explanation: Three out of four is more than half, so 'the majority' is the correct label.

gaps.sentence: She has ___ patience with rude customers.
Don't worry, we still have ___ time before the gates close.
gaps.hint: positive meaning: there is some time; 'time' is uncountable
gaps.explanation: 'A little time' means some time, which reassures; 'time' is uncountable.
